title: Paid orders per customer
statement:
Tables customers(id, name) and orders(id, customer_id, status), where status is 'paid' or 'cancelled'.

The goal: one row per customer with their name and their number of paid orders, showing 0 (not an empty value) for customers with no paid order, including customers with no order at all.

Which queries do that? Pick every one that applies.
choices:
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id)
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.id;

SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id)
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.id;

SELECT c.name, SUM(o.status = 'paid')
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id;

SELECT c.name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o
        WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid')
FROM customers c;
